<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a40eb02e83b660b7f05fa642890bb95e029f1178`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a40eb02e83b660b7f05fa642890bb95e029f1178` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `07f8a7d314839655e6adfa5d671d3727b71c6317` — the merge of head `61481ad4373931a8112d1374557057543d92415a` into base `a40eb02e83b660b7f05fa642890bb95e029f1178`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 07f8a7d314839655e6adfa5d671d3727b71c6317 && git checkout 07f8a7d314839655e6adfa5d671d3727b71c6317
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a40eb02e83b660b7f05fa642890bb95e029f1178 61481ad4373931a8112d1374557057543d92415a && git checkout -B drift-repro a40eb02e83b660b7f05fa642890bb95e029f1178 && git merge --no-ff 61481ad4373931a8112d1374557057543d92415a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a40eb02e83b660b7f05fa642890bb95e029f1178
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a40eb02e83b660b7f05fa642890bb95e029f1178` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `61481ad4373931a8112d1374557057543d92415a`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #31420 (body, triage `6718966345`, claim `6719078548`, os-dev-report `6719827836`), the PR #31464 body and its 6-file list, the net diff `origin/main...61481ad4`, and the head's check-runs. Every completed check-run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, all four `Type Check ·` jobs, `Test Core (1/8)`–`(8/8)` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are green. The UI and opt-in jobs are skipped because the diff does not touch them.

- **Public surface, package root `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (widening): right.** `index.ts` adds four named exports, nothing by `*`: the runtime function `answerOneTimeTokenHandoff` and the types `OneTimeTokenHandoffManager`, `OneTimeTokenHandoffServing` and `HandoffAnswer`. Each name and member matches the card's Ask 1 exactly: the four manager methods, the four serving members with `serverEnv?` optional, and `request` as `{ url, headers, queries }` with `queries` a record of string to readonly string array. `HandoffAnswer` is the module's existing interface (`status: 302 | 400 | 401 | 500`, `body?`, `headers`), now reachable from the root. Nothing leaves the root. `AuthManager` satisfies the manager shape structurally (its `getApi()` resolves to better-auth's `api`, assignable to the declared promise of `unknown`). The test's annotated `const handedManager: OneTimeTokenHandoffManager = manager` and the green `Type Check ·` jobs hold that.
- **Minting seams stay unpublished: right.** `runOneTimeTokenHandoff`, `withHandoffChallenge`, `resolveHandoffSignInEntry` and `oneTimeTokenStoreHasher` remain module-level exports only. Test 4 pins them out of `Object.keys(packageRoot)`. The only way into minting from the root is the whole answer, which calls `runOneTimeTokenHandoff` → `withHandoffChallenge` itself. That is the card's design constraint, and the claim's ⛔ on exporting the seams is respected.
- **Accept set of `GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff` on AuthPlugin's own mount (unchanged): right.** The route body moves verbatim into `answerOneTimeTokenHandoff`. `registeredSchemes`, `sessionCreatedAt` and `generate` are read off the same manager. `signInEntry` passes the same `signInPageUrl` (`getConsoleUrl('/login')`), `authBaseUrl` (`getAuthIssuer()`), `authMountPath: basePath`, `requestUrl: c.req.url`, `requestHost` (from the headers `runOneTimeTokenHandoff` hands it, the same `c.req.raw.headers`), `server: rawApp`, `serverEnv: c.env` and the same once-only `onUnserved` warn closure. `queries` and `headers` reach `runOneTimeTokenHandoff` as before. The `302`/JSON translation and the `500` catch in `auth-plugin.ts` are untouched, and the call is still inside the `try`. No answer of the existing route moves. The existing hand-off cases in the file are unchanged and green on `Test Core`.
- **Accept set for a forwarding host (new, from 404 to the hand-off): right.** A host that serves no AuthPlugin routes can now answer the route for a manager it did not mount. The new `describe` runs on a Hono host with no AuthPlugin constructed, at an origin other than the manager's `baseUrl`. It shows the card's Ask 3 matrix:
  - an anonymous JSON probe gets 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` and nothing is minted;
  - a signed-out navigation gets a 302 to the host's own `/_console/login`, root-relative, with `redirect` naming the same request;
  - a signed-in navigation gets a 302 to the app scheme, and `T.verifier` redeems 200 once, while the replay gets 400 `Invalid token`;
  - no stdout, stderr, console or `onUnserved` line carries the token.
  
  The ablation in the PR body (mint outside `withHandoffChallenge` turns case 3 red on the redeem row) meets the card's "goes red if the function mints outside the challenge scope". The spies are restored by the file's `afterEach(vi.restoreAllMocks)`.
- **Ledger row (`auth-route-ledger.ts`): right.** The note on `GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff` gains the forwarding-host sentence (Ask 4). Its `disposition: 'server-only'`, `source` and `requires` are unchanged, and the mount-ledger family is green inside `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- **Acceptance "in the published `index.d.ts`": met.** It is a named root export, and the `Type Check · consumer gates` job (dts closure) is green on this head.
- nit (no effect on the contract): `answerOneTimeTokenHandoff` is a plain function that returns a Promise. A synchronous throw from `manager.getRegisteredAppSchemes()` (on `AuthManager`, `registeredAppSchemesOf` → `assertTrustedAppSchemes`) would therefore escape as a throw instead of a rejection. AuthPlugin's call sits inside `try`, and `AuthManager` validates `trustedAppSchemes` at construction, so neither caller sees it today. Making the function `async` would give a host the rejection the `Promise` signature implies.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/31420-one-time-token-handoff-export.md` names `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch`, the one released package the diff moves. No `skip-changeset` is used, and none could be: the diff publishes.
- **Clause-②: `yes (widening)`, right.** It appears line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body. The diff adds one runtime export and three type exports to a published entry, so it widens the public surface. Nothing is removed or narrowed, so the arm is not `(narrowing)`. The card's Ask 5 `Clause-②: no` was wrong for this diff. The correction to `yes (widening)` is the right reading on its own merits, judged here against the diff and not adopted from the seat's claim.
- **Metadata-protocol: `none`, right.** No spec key, accepted value or metadata type moves, and `packages/spec/**` is untouched.
- **Level: `patch`, right.** Under AGENTS.md's rule the level follows the kind alone. A `Metadata-protocol: none` change, widening included, ships `patch`. Nothing is breaking, so no BREAKING banner, migration block or ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- `deviations`: "None to the card's shape". The diff confirms it, member by member (①). The other entry concerns process, not the contract: `pr_create` was opened with no assignees and no labels, following the order over os-dev.md rule 2. That is answered: it moves nothing a consumer sees.
- Card-versus-PR difference: Ask 5's `Clause-②: no` against the shipped `yes (widening)`. This is answered in ②: the shipped line is the correct one for the diff.
- Serial constraint: #30959 and #30967 also edit `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/**`. The PR states the rule (whichever lands later merges `origin/main` once and re-runs the plugin-auth suite). Head `61481ad4` already carries one merge of `origin/main` (`4941c40b`, including #31419's plugin-auth lockout work), and `Test Core` is green on it. This is answered and needs no escalation. The rule still binds whichever of the three lands last.
- Governed surface: none. `packages/spec/**` is not touched, no governed path is in the 6-file list, and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green. That is consistent with the `TIER_DEFAULT` declaration face.
- `security_findings`: none. The forwarding host still cannot mint outside the challenge scope (①), and test 3 asserts that the token reaches no log line.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mrhms6`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
